products.name: Hour One
products.note: AI avatar video; virtual presenters; enterprise video; likeness consent; Israeli vendor

reading.body:
Hour One is an Israeli vendor selling AI avatar video and virtual presenters for enterprise use, with likeness consent noted as part of the product.

The company sits in video generation, a category where the output is rendered frames rather than text. That distinction matters for the compute thesis because inference for video is continuous and heavy, and the data here does not say which models Hour One runs, whether it trains its own, or where the compute comes from. The note on likeness consent signals that the product depends on real people's faces, which is a legal and trust constraint rather than a power one.

What the record does not cover is scale. There is no funding figure, no customer count, no GPU count, no data center location, and no energy contract. For a site arguing that buildings and power bind AI scaling, this entry establishes only that the company exists, what it sells, and that it handles likeness rights. It cannot support any claim about how much compute Hour One consumes or where that compute is sited.
